.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r2/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md:9-11 (check 1 verify/defect) and block A context lines 1-36
evidence: Read cold, task/instruction.md is a first-person product ask from a recruiting team member, written as connected prose with no numbered acceptance list, no shall/must table, no feature matrix. Line 1: 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day? ... the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts.' Lines 3-9 describe needs as lived experience ('I often move several candidates together; that has to be all of them or none', 'leave my place, my draft and my cursor alone and just tell me there is something new', 'They must never see our internal notes, why someone was rejected, or anyone else'). Line 11 explicitly leaves design open ('layout and names are yours') and delegates exact rules to a notes file. The skill defect pattern 'build recipe (framework, file layout, endpoint list)' (quality-checks.md:11) was checked against line 13: it names Node.js/Express/SQLite, /app/server.js, port 3000, GET /api/health and /app/app.db, but these are the template-mandated shared runtime contract (identical to template environment/instructions/integration.md and required by check 4), stated once in a single conversational paragraph, and the brief expressly declines to prescribe layout: 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call.' It contains no endpoint list beyond the mandated health check and no step-by-step build order, so it is not a recipe. Lines 15-17 (seed loading, accounts) are likewise necessary contract facts in plain speech. The supporting note hireops_rules.md is detailed (role table at :14, HTTP codes 401/403/404 at :21-23, 409 at :78, 'Follow them exactly' at :3, a runtime-paths section at :195) and reads more like a team's working-rules document than a chat message; that is the intended /instructions notes mechanism of the template, it still frames itself in team voice ('our recruiting workspace', 'Routes, field names, element ids, button labels and the shape of the pages are yours') and is not a numbered acceptance checklist or build recipe. Recorded here as context only; voice consistency between brief and notes is row 2's scope, not a defect for row 1. Counterexample attempts: (a) a weak app passing because of this row is not applicable—row 1 concerns prompt form, not grading; (b) a conforming alternative failing due to over-prescription: the brief frees routes, file layout, names, layout, and transport (rules :3-4 and :123 'Polling, server-sent events and sockets are all acceptable'), so a differently structured but conforming app is not excluded by the instruction's wording. No runtime evidence is needed for this source-only row; nothing measured is being claimed.
